hello! I'm getting back into Lean after about 11 years since I took the CMU course back in 2015 (my project was this very ugly proof of bezout's identity in number theory that I'm still very proud of)

So it was cool to see the meteoric rise of Lean since then - and with AI assistance now the activation energy is low enough for me to explore a backlog of ideas. I'm especially interested in Lean as an application programming language for distributed systems with gRPC. The compelling angle for me is that protobuf as a type system sits right at the boundary of exact types, with some diligent design choices to fight against latent type structure. So I think of this as the ideal boundary for data if the programming language can faithfully represent all the relations that need to be stripped out of the type for serialization.
I've gotten it working as a C++ gRPC server, with types and bindings to/from Lean, and a protoc plugin generating all the glue. Plus libpqxx bindings on the other end to make it a toy API (eventually want to generate refinements from SQL constraints)

With the reality of autoregressive LLMs writing code this kind of stuff feels more worthwhile to explore - enforcing invariants end-to-end in the application layer and using codegen to hide the rough edges
Hello! I'm not sure I understand, did you implement Lean bindings for protobuf using an LLM? If so, how does this compare to https://github.com/Lean-zh/protobuf ?

first time seeing it! but that looks like a native wire implementation from Lean which is much more ambitious - I'm using the C++ library and effectively wrapping the message types in Lean
But since I wanted the gRPC server library as well it would have been a long road to a pure Lean version
Perhaps I should see if I can get Google to provide an official protobuf library for Lean...

i have not - this was my first attempt at something other than theorems
I could see that being useful for direct postgres i/o if there's not a Lean implementation already
I am a big fan of R2DBC for async database stuff elsewhere

Perhaps I should see if I can get Google to provide an official protobuf library for Lean...

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf#protobuf-runtime-installation looks very much centered around the google3 officially supported list of languages (I assume it still exists, I left in 2021) plus a very few odd ones. Unless someone internally is very interested in building lean software for the verified software aspects, it doesn't seem likely (no harm in asking). Do bazel lean rules exist?
Protobuf does has a knack to use resources from the work folder and stage while building so this requires interest.
I made a rules_lean for this project, would be happy to put it up somewhere

Might come in handy in a large multi-language project somewhere. Does the compiler run per lean_library or they just aggregate files for one big run at lean_binary (I used to work on typescript rules). Is there something like header files in lean (I know very little about the compilation model)
there are olean files as the compiler output, where I think the closest analogy is a .o with some Lean-specific metadata
But those always change, so if you edit a private def in a file the .o would change but the header shouldn’t hence not retriggering a recombination downstream

it looks like it's a bit nuanced in the lean_library case and essentially amounts to: there's an option for whether to compile into a static library or .so via lean's intermediate c outputs (actual .o files)

but it's not required, if Bazel just collects the transitive dependencies of all the intermediate libraries in a tree, it definitely doesn't need all the static libraries along the way - it's a flag here but it could be an optional output group or similar

the transitive invalidation picture on olean files should just line up with lean's behavior directly I think

Missing from those providers is tracking public / private scope, which I have a prototype of
